precepts.text: Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion. So that goes with the marriage supper of the Lamb, which Christians say, oh, we are going to be in the marriage feast. No, you are not. None of you Catholics, you Baptists, you Episcopalians, you Anglicans, you Muslims and Mormons, you are not going to be there.
precepts.point: But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For thy Maker is thine husband”. That Maker is Christ: “the Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel”. So the Lord was never married to all nations on the earth. He was only married to Israel, and Jeremiah says so: “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion”.

He is married to the backsliding children of Israel, and he calls them to turn. That is why Isaiah 54:6 speaks of “a wife of youth, when thou wast refused”: refused because we were sinning. He said return, for I am married unto you, and we did not want to return, so the Most High refused us.

And that goes with the marriage supper of the Lamb, where Christians say, oh, we are going to be in the marriage feast. No, you are not. None of you Catholics, you Baptists, you Episcopalians, you Anglicans, you Muslims and Mormons, you are not going to be there. The Lord is married to Israel, and it is Israel he takes, one of a city and two of a family, and brings to Zion.

We are lacking everything. Pastors after God's heart, feeding us the laws, are the shepherds who end that lack.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Israel is found “Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth”. The stock is a piece of wood, a wooden god. The stone is the Kaaba stone, the black stone in Mecca that people come from all around the world to kiss, revered as a relic from heaven. To say to that stone, you brought me forth, is to say, you created me.

The Lord says why: “for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.” Then the Lord answers: “But where are thy gods that thou hast made thee? let them arise, if they can save thee in the time of thy trouble”. Where is the Kaaba stone that you made? Where is the wooden god that you made? Let them rise up and save you.

Then: “for according to the number of thy cities are thy gods, O Judah.” We started to worship many gods, and Allah was one of them, around 639 AD. That is the harlotry of Jeremiah 3:1-3: Israel “played the harlot with many lovers”, sat for them “as the Arabian in the wilderness” when the Arabs came conquering and forcing Islam on our people all through North Africa, and then we forced it on our own people too.

So the “whore’s forehead” of verse 3 is plain to see: the dark prayer mark worn on the forehead from bowing the head to the ground before that other god. And yet the people call it Islam and hold it up as good for the black man. Your fellow Arab Muslims are selling our people on open slave markets, and a stone cannot save you in the time of your trouble.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
God’s law says it plainly: “Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.” Make no idols, no graven images, and no image of stone to bow down to.

This is what our people do. We go all the way to Mecca to kiss a rock, the Kaaba stone. And they say, we don’t worship the Kaaba stone. Yes, you do. Their own ruling says it: kissing the black stone is an act of worship, done by a Muslim who has no connection to that stone except worshiping Allah by venerating it and following the messenger by doing it. That is bowing down to an image of stone, the very thing the law forbids.

Mecca itself was run down and raggedy in the first known photograph of the Kaaba in 1861. Then they started working with America on oil and got paid, and now people from all over the world call it beautiful. It is still a stone set up to bow down unto.

So Leviticus 26:1 shows why Jeremiah 3 calls it harlotry and polluting the land, and why Israel has a “whore’s forehead” and refuses “to be ashamed”. The Most High is the Lord our God, and he is not in a black stone in Arabia.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
God says, “And I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”. The flock has been scattered in all countries since the time of slavery: from the Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians and Medes, Greeks and Romans, to Spain, France, England and now America. God drove them there, and he will “bring them again to their folds”, their tribes, “and they shall be fruitful and increase.”

“And I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them”. Feed them what? Grits and honey? Pork chops and chitlins? No. Jeremiah 3:15 tells what they will be fed: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

That is the difference between the pastors of Jeremiah 23 who scatter and the shepherds God sets up. The shepherds feed the people with knowledge and understanding, and then “they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking, saith the Lord.”

precepts.text: I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding. note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge.” Where is that knowledge going to come from? From the leadership. Jeremiah shows it: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Your pastors could have been the negroes in the world, leaders who just seek after covetousness. But the Lord led you to pastors according to his heart, brothers who are able to help you build and help you see yourself. They feed you with knowledge and understanding, so that is who you seek after.

So why do you keep running away from them? On the quests there are brothers who show up just to have fun. You see them once, turn around, and they are gone for days: they were not on the quest, they were on a cruise. They are not going for any wisdom, knowledge or understanding whatsoever.

That is the fool of Proverbs 15, whose mouth “feedeth on foolishness”: when leadership is in the room, he looks for who he can talk sports or his job with. The man who has understanding seeks the war room and seeks the water from the Bishop, the Deacons, the captains and the officers. That is what leadership is there for, and this whole Bible is about knowledge, wisdom and understanding that we have to seek out.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with. In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness; and thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy wickedness.” The Most High is speaking to Israel, and He speaks to her as the woman.

That shows who the woman is in Genesis 3:15. This is a prophecy, not the serpent and Eve: the woman is the nation of Israel. And the woman does not plant seed, the man plants seed, so the Most High is saying He will put enmity between Satan's seed and Israel's seed, and that enmity remains. Christ was to come from the woman, and Revelation 12 explains this verse.

Bruising the heel is making Israel stumble. When a serpent strikes at your heel you stumble; Satan makes Israel stumble through evil communication and corrupting good manners.

precepts.text: If a man put away his wife and she become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?
precepts.point: The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

note.label: Deuteronomy 24: Divorcement, Pledges, and Mercy to the Poor

precepts.why:
The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again. The law answers: “Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the Lord: and thou shalt not cause the land to sin”.

The prophet asks the same thing out of this law: “They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?” The land greatly polluted in Jeremiah is the land caused to sin here; the answer to his question is this law, and it is no.

precepts.text: If a man put away his wife and she become another man's, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

note.label: Jeremiah 3: Backsliding Israel Called to Return

precepts.why:
The Lord promises to give “pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.” Malachi shows what that knowledge is: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

Knowledge is God's laws. The people are to seek the law at the priest's mouth, so a pastor according to his heart is one who feeds us with the laws of God. If your pastor is not feeding you God's laws, you need to run. The pastor he gives to the backsliding children he brings to Zion is the messenger of the Lord of hosts, and his lips keep the law.

note.label: Jeremiah 4: Return unto Me, or Destruction from the North

precepts.why:
“If thou wilt return, O Israel, saith the Lord, return unto me”. The chapter before shows what kind of return this is: “They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the Lord.”

The Most High uses the analogy of a man who puts away his wife and she becomes another man's. Israel played the harlot with many lovers, the nations, and by that rule the land is greatly polluted; yet he still says, return again to me. If Israel returns and puts away their abominations out of his sight, they shall not be removed out of their land.

precepts.text: Israel played the harlot with many lovers, yet the Most High still calls her to return again to him.
precepts.point: He will not have mercy upon her children, for they be children of whoredoms, and their mother has played the harlot, saying she will go after her lovers that give her bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink. This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them.

note.label: Hosea 2: Plead With Your Mother

precepts.why:
Israel’s mother “hath played the harlot”, saying “I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.” This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them. Jeremiah says the same: “thou hast played the harlot with many lovers”.

Yet notice what follows. “If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?” Even so, “yet return again to me, saith the Lord.” Israel played the harlot with many lovers, and the Most High still calls her to return again to him.

precepts.text: For all the causes whereby backsliding Israel committed adultery, he put her away and gave her a bill of divorcement, and her treacherous sister Judah followed and played the harlot also.
precepts.point: He will not have mercy upon her children, for they be children of whoredoms, and their mother has played the harlot, saying she will go after her lovers that give her bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink. This is Israel following the other nations that ruled over them.

note.label: Hosea 2: Plead With Your Mother

precepts.why:
“For their mother hath played the harlot: she that conceived them hath done shamefully”. Jeremiah shows the Most High’s answer to that harlotry: “for all the causes whereby backsliding Israel committed adultery I had put her away, and given her a bill of divorce”. He put Israel away for going after her lovers, the other nations that ruled over them.

And it did not stop there: “yet her treacherous sister Judah feared not, but went and played the harlot also.” Judah followed Israel and played the harlot too.
